zh.h1: 我如何重新梳理跨裝置、跨系統的同步管理體驗
zh.sum: 此專案展現我如何從表層回饋中挖掘真正的產品問題，重新梳理流程結構，並推動更符合使用者理解的體驗優化。
zh.metaTeam:
專案經理 ×1
產品設計師 ×1
軟體工程師 ×3（前端、後端、AI）
zh.metaRole:
產品設計師
負責釐清問題、整合利害關係人回饋，並重構流程與介面優化
zh.bgLead: 從用戶回饋中拆解問題，推動產品從表層介面修補，<br class="cs-bp">轉向同步架構與流程的重新檢視
zh.bgP1: 由於此功能需支援機器人與多個任務、團隊群組之間的同步、權限控管與內容更新，同時牽涉跨裝置的資訊呈現與任務狀態管理，因此實際問題比表面所見更加複雜，也不容易在產品初期被察覺。
zh.bgP2: 因此產品上線約兩年後，隨著使用者與應用情境逐漸增加，原先隱藏的問題才陸續浮現。我在彙整大量使用者回饋與操作情境後，進一步釐清問題並非源自單一介面或個別功能，而是前期在同步架構與操作流程上的規劃不足。
zh.bgP3: 這些底層邏輯未能透過介面清楚傳達，導致使用者無法正確理解機器人的當前狀態、任務之間的關聯，以及操作後可能產生的影響。當實際結果不符合使用者預期時，便容易被視為產品異常，進而降低使用者對系統的理解與信任。
zh.resLead: 我整合 RD、客服與用戶回饋，<br class="cs-bp">從矛盾訊號中釐清真正的 UX 痛點
zh.q1: 大量客人反應機器人大腦有異常，提交給相關部門後卻告知我們大腦正常。
zh.q2: 經常花大量時間排查問題，但結果又跟客戶的說法有出入。
zh.q3: 明明取消專案了，機器人怎麼還回話，讓客人接收到已過期的優惠價格。
zh.probLead: 我發現同步流程的系統邏輯，<br class="cs-bp">與用戶對操作結果的預期存在落差
zh.probD1: 使用者無法在操作前確認同步會影響哪些任務與裝置，難以預測操作後的結果。
zh.probT2: 同步規則缺乏明確說明
zh.probD2: 系統未清楚說明同步條件與狀態變化，增加操作結果的不確定性，也降低使用者的操作信心。
zh.probT3: 取消同步後狀態不一致
zh.probD3: 前端操作與後端資料狀態未能一致更新，導致使用者誤以為同步失敗或機器人發生故障。
zh.stratLead: 對齊系統邏輯與用戶預期，建立可信任的同步體驗
zh.stratBody: 我重新梳理產品流程與同步規則，釐清裝置、任務與團隊群組之間的系統關係，並對齊系統行為、用戶預期與介面回饋，讓操作結果清楚可預期，重建用戶對產品的信任。
zh.stratD1: 重構流程對齊 User 的操作預期，並視覺化同步狀態。
zh.stratD2: 整合不同裝置中的同步資訊呈現與任務狀態。
zh.stratD3: 將同步取消後的規則從「遞補」改為「淨空」，避免不明干擾。
zh.solLead: 讓每一次同步操作，<br class="cs-bp">都能被看見、被預期、被信任
zh.solPhSmall: 金絲桃另製流程圖後補上圖素與說明，此處僅預留空間
zh.takeP1: 此次產品優化的核心能力，是將看不見的系統行為轉化為用戶能理解、能預期的回饋。
zh.takeP2: 我建立起以系統視角進行 UX 規劃的方法，透過用戶回饋逐步釐清問題，並在跨裝置、多專案與機器人端的複雜情境中，將零散的操作痛點回推到規則層，解決真正的系統狀態與流程問題，進一步提升系統穩定性與用戶信任。
zh.takeD1: 讓操作行為與預期一致，建立用戶信心，讓規則被看見。
zh.takeD2: 對齊使用者的操作預期，並重新定義後端對資料的處理方式。
zh.takeD3: 減少人工排查問題的時間，同時降低反覆的溝通成本。

en.h1: How I rethought sync management across devices and systems
en.sum: This project shows how I dug beneath surface-level feedback to uncover the real product problems — restructuring flows and driving experience improvements that match how users actually think.
en.metaRole:
Product Designer
Defining the problem, synthesising stakeholder feedback, and restructuring the flow and interface
en.bgLead: Digging beneath user feedback to re-examine the sync architecture and flow
en.bgP1: Because the feature had to support syncing, permission control, and content updates across robots, multiple tasks, and team groups — while also handling cross-device information display and task state — the real problem ran deeper than it appeared, and was hard to spot in the product's early stages.
en.bgP2: About two years after launch, as users and use cases grew, the hidden issues began to surface. After gathering extensive user feedback and usage scenarios, I clarified that the problem didn't stem from a single screen or feature — it came from insufficient planning of the sync architecture and operational flow early on.
en.bgP3: The underlying logic was never clearly conveyed through the interface, leaving users unable to understand the robot's current state, how tasks related to one another, or what their actions would cause. When results didn't match expectations, it read as a product malfunction — eroding users' understanding of and trust in the system.
en.resLead: I brought together feedback from RD, customer support, and users — finding the real UX pain points inside contradictory signals
en.q1: Customers keep reporting the robot's brain is faulty — but every time we escalate it, we're told the brain is fine.
en.q2: We spend hours debugging, and the findings still don't match what the customer describes.
en.q3: I cancelled the project, so why is the robot still replying — and quoting expired promotional prices to my customers?
en.probLead: I found a gap between the system logic of the sync flow and what users expected their actions to do
en.probD1: Users couldn't confirm which tasks and devices a sync would affect before acting, making outcomes hard to predict.
en.probD2: The system never spelled out sync conditions or state changes, adding uncertainty and lowering users' confidence.
en.probD3: Frontend actions and backend data didn't update in step, so users assumed the sync had failed or the robot was broken.
en.stratLead: Aligning system logic with user expectations to build trust
en.stratBody: I restructured the product flow and sync rules, clarified how devices, tasks, and team groups relate to one another, and aligned system behaviour, user expectations, and interface feedback — making outcomes predictable and rebuilding trust in the product.
en.stratD1: Restructured the flow around users' expectations and made sync status visible.
en.stratD2: Consolidated how sync information and task status appear across devices.
en.stratD3: Changed post-cancellation behaviour from "backfill" to "clear", removing unexplained interference.
en.solLead: Making every sync visible, predictable, and trustworthy
en.solPhSmall: Flow diagrams and captions will be added later — this space is reserved
en.takeP1: The core capability behind this optimisation was turning invisible system behaviour into feedback users can understand and anticipate.
en.takeP2: I built a way of approaching UX from a systems perspective — using user feedback to clarify the problem step by step, and tracing scattered pain points back to the rule layer across a complex landscape of devices, projects, and robot endpoints — resolving the underlying state and flow issues, and strengthening both system stability and user trust.
en.takeD1: Actions now match outcomes, building confidence and making the rules visible.
en.takeD2: Aligned with user expectations and redefined how the backend handles data.
en.takeD3: Less time spent manually debugging, and fewer repeated rounds of communication.
